name: Mirage MPK runtime and scheduler
scope: Static reading of the Mirage Persistent Kernel runtime checked out at agent_space/mirage (commit f9eb70c, 2026-10-05). Files read: include/mirage/persistent_kernel/runtime_header.h, persistent_kernel.cuh (worker loop, scheduler loop, init and prepare kernels, prepare_next_batch, launch); src/kernel/runtime.cc (register_mugraph task and event emission, prelaunch conversion); src/kernel/annotated_graph.cc and its header (per-edge GCD event_dim, fork/join LCM); src/kernel/task_register.cc (Hopper swapAB linear codegen); python/mirage/mpk/persistent_kernel.py, mpk.py, models/qwen3/builder.py, models/utils.py, python/mirage/utils.py (worker/scheduler sizing). Also read the MPK paper (arXiv 2512.22219v2, OSDI'26). On the MegaBake side: src/megabake/runtime.py, schedule.py, codegen.py (table driver loop), compiler.py (table-launch and scheduler selection), plan.py, bodies/gemm.py, buckets.py, ROADMAP.md, PERFORMANCE_REPORT.md, and artifacts/full_model_2026-10-18/*/report.json. Question answered: how MPK synchronizes and dispatches tasks without grid barriers, how it handles serving state on the GPU, which parts MegaBake already has, which it lacks, and what closing the runtime gap would gain on the 60-SM H200 MIG slice. No GPU jobs were run.

core_ideas.how_it_works: The grid is num_workers + num_schedulers/4 CTAs (persistent_checker asserts this). CTAs with blockIdx < num_workers run execute_worker, each owning one task queue, and each holds one SM because of __launch_bounds__(WORKER_NUM_THREADS,1) and large dynamic shared memory. The remaining CTAs run execute_scheduler: lane 0 of each of the first 4 warps is one scheduler with its own event queue. A shared global queue (index num_schedulers) carries broadcast events. Workers and schedulers can also run as two kernels on two streams (split_worker_scheduler). The paper's sizing is 128 workers + 16 scheduler warps (4 SMs) on H100. The repository's get_configurations_from_gpu instead maps >=40 SMs to 30 workers and 4*(sm-30) schedulers, so a 60-SM slice would give 30 SMs to schedulers.

core_ideas.idea: SM-level task graph with tile-granular events (trigger_event / dependent_event counters)
core_ideas.how_it_works: Each operator (a KN customized op with a bgraph grid_dim) expands into one task per block id. An edge's events are not per operator. event_dim is gcd(producer partition, consumer partition) along each tensor dim, so a consumer task waits only for the producer tasks that write the slice it reads. Fork and join points unify partitions with an LCM pass, and view-induced edges degrade to one event. Every task stores one trigger_event, which it increments after finishing, and one dependent_event, which it waits on before starting. An EventDesc holds num_triggers and a contiguous [first_task_id,last_task_id) consumer range, produced by linearizing task emission order. The paper reports that this event fusion cuts events 37-118x, to 1,142-2,366 events encoding 69k-162k task-pair dependencies.

core_ideas.idea: Monotonic, never-reset event counters keyed by iteration number
core_ideas.how_it_works: A TaskId packs iteration<<32 | index. On completion, a worker issues atom.add.release.gpu on all_event_counters[e]. The event is ready when count == num_triggers * iteration, so counters are never reset between decode iterations and need no extra fence or reset phase. Waiters poll with ld.acquire (sys scope) plus __nanosleep(10). NVSHMEM events use nvshmem_signal_wait_until on the same counter.

core_ideas.idea: Static AOT prelaunch: the whole iteration's tasks are dispatched round-robin up front, and workers wait locally
core_ideas.how_it_works: After building the graph, register_mugraph rewrites every LAUNCH_TASKS/LAUNCH_MASSIVE_TASKS event into EVENT_EMPTY and sets dependent_event on its consumer tasks. Event 1, the begin-graph event (LAUNCH_DEPENDENT_TASKS), then covers tasks [2, N). When it fires, the local schedulers split the range and write task ids round-robin into worker queues, so task k goes roughly to worker k mod W. Each worker runs its queue in order. It batch-loads up to 16 TaskDescs into shared memory with cp.async, spins on each task's dependent_event, runs it, and bumps trigger_event. Completed events no longer go through a scheduler. Schedulers only handle END_OF_TASK_GRAPH and the next iteration. Correctness relies on the emission order being topological by depth. The paper describes a hybrid JIT/AOT mode in which workers prefer scheduler-assigned JIT tasks, plus paged 32 KB shared-memory pages for cross-task prefetch. Neither appears in this checkout: no JIT queue code and no smem-page code was found.

Synchronization is only point-to-point event counters. Iteration boundaries use the END_OF_TASK_GRAPH event, which every leaf task triggers. Scheduler 0 then runs prepare_next_batch and enqueues the begin-graph task with iteration+1. Because counters are monotonic, early tasks of iteration i+1 can start as soon as their own inputs are ready.

core_ideas.idea: On-GPU serving loop: continuous batching, chunked prefill, paged KV allocator, runtime token counts
core_ideas.how_it_works: prepare_next_batch runs single-threaded on a scheduler warp between iterations. It commits output tokens, detects EOS or max length, frees KV pages back into a ring page_queue, compacts request slots, and admits new requests. It caps prefill chunks by MPK_TOKEN_ROOM(MPK_MAX_NUM_BATCHED_TOKENS) and rebuilds qo_indptr, paged_kv_indptr/indices/last_page_len per KV group (sliding windows supported). The task graph is compiled for the maximum batch tokens. Tasks read qo_indptr and step at runtime, so the token count is a device value, not a recompile or padding bucket. The paper also mentions power-of-two batch-size ttGraphs selected at runtime. This checkout hardcodes num_graphs=1.

core_ideas.idea: Host-device interaction through pinned lock-free rings (one launch for a whole generation)
core_ideas.how_it_works: In offline mode one kernel launch runs every decode iteration until all requests finish. In MODE_ONLINE_PINNED the CPU writes requests into a pinned ring (ready flag with release semantics) and the GPU consumes them with ld.acquire.sys. The GPU publishes per-row progress (pinned_step) and completions with st.release.sys for CPU streaming, and a pinned shutdown flag ends the kernel. The host never launches per step.

core_ideas.idea: Multi-GPU inside the megakernel via NVSHMEM
core_ideas.how_it_works: Event ids carry an NVSHMEM tag and a target GPU. Workers have a second remote queue fed by remote schedulers. AllReduce is a task (TASK_NVSHMEM_TILE_ALLREDUCE) using nvshmemx tile_sum_reduce_block with NVLS one-shot pull. In the paper, AllReduce is decomposed into signal-wait transfer tasks plus local reduce tasks that overlap with compute. Buffers come from nvshmem_malloc when USE_NVSHMEM is defined.

core_ideas.idea: Operator fusion into few task types per layer, with linears split into a multiple of the worker count
core_ideas.how_it_works: A Qwen3 decode layer on Hopper has about 8 task layers: rmsnorm, fused qkv linear, paged attention (with RoPE and qk-norm), o_proj linear_with_residual, rmsnorm, fused gate_up linear, silu_mul, down linear_with_residual. Linears use 64 or 96 tasks (grid_for_rmsnorm_linear_layer), so every operator has many independent tiles and events can overlap neighbouring operators. The Hopper linear is swapAB with batch <= 16.

Only whole-region events are code-generated, and only in the per-tensor-parameter module. megabake_status.idea: Monotonic, never-reset event counters keyed by iteration number
megabake_status.evidence: src/megabake/runtime.py:111-134 (counting_grid_barrier uses (ordinal+1)*workers), :227-247 (wait_for_event uses (epoch+1)*trigger_count); call counter in ready buffer (runtime.py:42-48)
megabake_status.notes: The same idea is used for barriers and region events. Differences: wait_for_event polls with atomic_cas, a read-modify-write, where MPK uses ld.acquire plus nanosleep. MegaBake keeps int32 counters and resets before wrap, where MPK uses u64. Switching wait_for_event to an acquire load reduces L2 atomic contention when many CTAs poll one counter.

megabake_status.idea: Static AOT prelaunch: the whole iteration's tasks are dispatched round-robin up front, and workers wait locally
megabake_status.evidence: src/megabake/schedule.py:514 (worker_id = order % workers, same as MPK); src/megabake/schedule.py:1510-1526 and codegen.py:1168-1180 (contiguous split plus CTA rotation per interval)
megabake_status.notes: The event schedule data structure matches MPK's AOT model (static per-worker task list, waits on counters). The emitted table kernel instead runs phase by phase: a CTA finishes all its tiles of phase p before p+1 and waits at each interval's barrier. MegaBake has no per-task descriptor table (phase_table rows are per phase, not per tile) and no shared-memory prefetch of upcoming descriptors.

For the stated goal (a generic compiler for HF/PyTorch models), a runtime token count (qo_indptr-style) matters most because it removes bucket padding (a 65-token prompt pays for 128).

megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.opportunity: Tile-granular cross-operator dependencies (consumer tile starts when only its producer tiles are done)
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.why_multikernel_cannot: Between kernels the dependency is kernel-complete. PDL (cudaGridDependencySynchronize / griddepcontrol) only lets the next kernel's prologue run early. Its main body still waits for the whole previous grid to trigger or exit, and it cannot express 'tile j of B depends on tiles 2j,2j+1 of A'. Stream-level concurrency needs independent kernels.
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.nearest_substitute: CUDA Graphs plus PDL hide launch latency (~0.8 us per kernel in the MPK paper) and overlap prologues (smem setup, descriptor prefetch). The kernel-wide tail of each operator remains. That tail is what MegaBake's grid barriers also pay today, so MegaBake gains nothing exclusive until step 10 lands.

megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.opportunity: Weight prefetch for the next operator while waiting on events (cross-task software pipelining)
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.why_multikernel_cannot: A later kernel's CTAs do not exist until the earlier kernel's CTAs retire (or, with PDL, its prologue can start but competes for SM residency). A resident CTA that knows its next task can issue cp.async.bulk.prefetch.L2 or TMA loads for its next weight tiles before the dependency is satisfied, because weights do not depend on activations. The MPK paper attributes a 1.2-1.3x speedup on the final linear (Qwen3-8B, B200) to this.
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.nearest_substitute: PDL with weight prefetch in the prologue before griddepcontrol.wait gets part of this, but only one kernel ahead and only if the next kernel is co-resident.

megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.opportunity: Overlap of under-filled operators (K/V projections, norms, attention over few heads) with other independent work
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.why_multikernel_cannot: Concurrent kernels on multiple streams can overlap, but the graph partitioner must prove independence. Each kernel still carries launch, drain and tail costs, and small kernels block SM slots unpredictably. In a megakernel, idle CTAs pull the next ready task from their static queue.
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.nearest_substitute: Multi-stream CUDA graphs with fork/join (Inductor does not do this by default). Horizontal fusion of independent GEMMs (q/k/v concatenation) is the practical substitute and also works in MegaBake.

megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.opportunity: Device-resident serving loop (batching, KV paging, sampling, stop detection) with zero host round trips per token
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.why_multikernel_cannot: A CUDA graph is fixed. Changing batch composition, sequence length or page tables per step needs a host decision or device-side graph launch. A persistent kernel can rebuild its own metadata between iterations and loop without returning.
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.nearest_substitute: CUDA graphs captured per batch size plus host-side scheduling (vLLM/SGLang), costing tens of microseconds of host work per step, overlapped through async scheduling. Device graph launch (cudaGraphLaunch from device) is a partial alternative with limits.

megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.opportunity: Compute-communication overlap at tile granularity (NVSHMEM signal per tile)
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.why_multikernel_cannot: NCCL collectives are separate kernels with whole-tensor granularity. Overlapping them needs streams and SM partitioning. Inside a megakernel a reduce task starts as soon as its tile's remote signal arrives. The MPK paper reports 1.1x per-iteration gain on Qwen3-1.7B with 4x H100.
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.nearest_substitute: Fused GEMM+AllReduce kernels (e.g. cuBLASMp, Flux, TransformerEngine userbuffers). Not relevant on a single MIG slice.

measured_or_reported_gains: MPK paper (arXiv 2512.22219v2): 1.0-1.7x lower end-to-end latency than vLLM/SGLang (with CUDA graphs) on A100/H100/B200, batch 1-16, 64-token prompts, 1,024 output tokens, bf16. Gains are largest for small models and newer GPUs. Qwen3-8B on A100 at batch 1: 14.5 -> 12.5 ms per token, against a ~10 ms weight-load floor. Multi-GPU Qwen3-1.7B TP on 8x H100: 1.1-1.4x over SGLang/vLLM. Ablations: in-kernel scheduler is 0.28% of runtime; cross-task pipelining speeds the final linear 1.2-1.3x (Qwen3-8B, B200); compute-communication overlap 1.1x (Qwen3-1.7B, 4x H100); event fusion 37-118x fewer events; launch overhead estimate for Qwen3-8B is 293 launches x 3.8 us = 1.1 ms eager, ~0.2 ms with CUDA graphs. The README states 1.2-6.7x over unspecified baselines [uncertain: baseline mix not stated]. MegaBake measured (artifacts/full_model_2026-10-18, H200 MIG 3g.71gb): decode kernel GPU time SmolLM-135M 1,502 us vs Inductor 1,382 us; SmolLM-1.7B 2,974 vs 2,425 us; Qwen2-0.5B 1,584 vs 1,636 us. Complete calls: 2,138 / 3,311 / 2,380 us vs Inductor 11,925 / 10,323 / 10,739 us. Qwen3.5-0.8B prefill: no MegaBake result. No MPK number exists for a 60-SM slice. MPK's own heuristic would run there with 30 workers.
expected_impact_on_megabake:
Ranked by expected decode gain on the 60-SM slice. Baselines: 1.7B kernel 2.97 ms (GEMMs ~1.92 ms at ~1.8 TB/s; weight floor ~1.5 ms), 135M kernel 1.50 ms (weight floor ~0.12 ms, so latency-bound).
(1) Events in the table launch, at phase level first (step 10). Removes about 150-180 counting barriers at 0.7 us, a direct 0.10-0.13 ms. More importantly, it removes the interval drain: phases with few tiles (K/V GEMMs on 3 of 60 CTAs, norms, attention) let other CTAs start the next independent or partially ready work. Estimate: 135M 1.50 -> 1.1-1.25 ms (-15-25%), 1.7B 2.97 -> 2.6-2.75 ms (-8-12%) [uncertain: depends on how much of the ~1.05 ms non-GEMM time on 1.7B is serial latency versus barrier wait; measure with tools/phase_profile.py stamps].
(2) Cross-phase L2 weight prefetch while waiting on events (step 9), which needs (1) to be useful. It lets GEMM phases start with warm L2, lifting effective GEMM bandwidth from ~1.8 toward ~2.0 TB/s: 1.7B GEMM time 1.92 -> ~1.7 ms, about -0.2 ms (-7%). Small effect on 135M (weights are only ~0.27 GB at bf16).
(3) Tile-granular events with GCD/LCM-style grouping. Beyond phase-level events this lets attention start per KV head as soon as that head's q/k/v tiles land, and lets o_proj start per head group. Estimate a further 3-8% on 135M, 2-4% on 1.7B [uncertain].
(4) Persistent multi-step decode loop with device sampling and stop flag. This is not kernel time but complete-call time: it removes ~0.36 ms MegaBake host work + ~0.29 ms Dynamo guards per token (about 0.6 ms of the 2.14 ms 135M call, ~28%; ~0.5 ms of the 3.31 ms 1.7B call, ~15%). Pipelined calls already hide part of this (1,498 us vs 2,135 us on 135M), so the real gain is the non-overlapped remainder.
(5) Runtime token count instead of buckets (qo_indptr-style). Prefill padding waste is up to 2x per bucket boundary (65 tokens paying for 128). That does not fix the 3-21x prefill gap, which comes from the prefill attention body and the >64-row GEMM path.
(6) Worker/scheduler split, paging, NVSHMEM: no gain on this hardware.
Combined realistic target after (1)-(3): 1.7B decode kernel ~2.3-2.5 ms, around Inductor's 2.42 ms. That is still short of ROADMAP's 2.0 ms goal without fused QKV/gate-up and epilogue fusions. 135M ~1.0-1.2 ms, beating Inductor's 1.38 ms kernels [uncertain].
generality_and_overfitting_risk:
MPK is not model-generic. Models are hand-written builders (python/mirage/mpk/models/qwen3/builder.py and others), and runtime_header.h:87-226 hardcodes per-model task types (Inkling, GLM, GPT-OSS, DeepSeek MLA TP2/4/8 variants). Grid sizes come from grid_for_rmsnorm_linear_layer (models/utils.py:3-15), whose comment says 96 and 64 were chosen to cover Qwen3. Split-K is only enabled on target_cc==100 (qwen3/builder.py:293). The Hopper linear asserts batch<=16 (task_register.cc:1634). The worker count comes from an SM-count lookup table (python/mirage/utils.py:33-53) that maps a 60-SM device to 30 workers and 120 schedulers, which is clearly not tuned for MIG slices. The runtime mechanism is generic: monotonic counters, GCD/LCM event derivation and AOT round-robin queues depend on no model or GPU. MegaBake should copy that and not the builders.
MegaBake items that look tuned to the tested models or the 60-SM slice: (a) bodies/gemm.py:1890-1893 SWAP_AB_MAX_ROWS=64, justified by a 60-SM measurement. (b) compiler.py:205-224 _TABLE_LAUNCH_OPS=1000 and 24,000-byte parameter estimate; this is a hard switch that decides whether events are available at all, so small graphs get events and full models do not. (c) schedule.py:1384-1386 _FOLD_MAX_ROUNDS_PER_PHASE=2, _FOLD_MAX_ROUNDS=6, _FOLD_MAX_PHASES=6, tuned on SmolLM decode (135M 333 -> 183 barriers). (d) bodies/gemm.py:1903-1905 SPLIT_K_MAX=16, SPLIT_K_MIN_K_TILES=2, plus split-K being off because it gave 'no gain on the 60-SM slice'; that conclusion may flip on 132-SM H100 where tiles < workers more often. (e) compiler.py:240-241 plan tolerances (1% / 2%), explained with the 30-layer SmolLM. (f) buckets.py:38 DEFAULT_BUCKETS (16..512). (g) The schedule.py:514 round-robin plus codegen.py:1168-1180 CTA rotation assume one CTA per SM (PERFORMANCE_REPORT notes 214 KB GEMM smem fixes occupancy at 1). Positives: plan.py:501-530 searches worker counts {W, W/2, W/4} from target.multiprocessor_count, and admit_runtime checks SM count. That is better than MPK's lookup table.
How to avoid overfitting: derive thresholds from TargetFacts (SM count, smem, bandwidth) through a small cost model, e.g. swapAB when rows <= the WGMMA N limit and weight-tile share per stage beats activation share. Measure candidates at compile time (plan.py already does this) instead of constants. Express fold limits in estimated microseconds versus measured barrier cost, not in rounds. Keep the events/barrier choice independent of the launch encoding, so the table launch carries events for every graph size.
hardware_portability: Portable to SM80/SM90/SM100 unchanged: monotonic event counters (atom.add.release / ld.acquire.gpu, scope gpu), static per-worker task queues, GCD/LCM event derivation, device-side batch metadata, pinned rings (ld.acquire.sys/st.release.sys need SM70+). They depend only on a co-resident grid, which cooperative launch or occupancy-sized grids provide. The scheduler warps need nothing special. SM90-specific pieces around the runtime are TMA descriptors stored per task (MPK keeps up to 3 TMA desc pointers per tensor in TaskDesc; MegaBake writes descriptors from the address table in the prologue), WGMMA swapAB bodies, setmaxnreg (MPK fixes registers at the max over all task types; MegaBake decreases registers in GEMM warps, which PERFORMANCE_REPORT item 11 flags as unverified when generic bodies follow), and cp.async.bulk.prefetch.L2 for cross-phase prefetch (SM90+; SM80 can use ordinary prefetch.global.L2 or cp.async). On SM100, CLC (cluster launch control) could replace static queues for dynamic tile stealing, and TMEM/tcgen05 change only bodies. MPK's SM100 paths add split-K and 2-CTA MMA. Keeping it target-generic: put the event table, counters and queue layout in plan/runtime with no architecture assumptions. Restrict per-target code to bodies (bodies/blackwell.py already exists). Use target-queried constants (SM count, smem, max active blocks), and pick the barrier-versus-event and prefetch strategy per target through a cost model, not fixed flags.

recommended_actions.action: Add event counters to the table launch at phase granularity: per-phase counter slots in the ready buffer, phase_table columns for (wait_event, wait_target_per_epoch, publish_event). The wait uses ld.acquire polling with nanosleep, not atomic_cas. Generate barriers only where storage reuse demands them (workspace lifetime ends). Make make_region_event_schedule the default for table launches.
recommended_actions.expected_gain: 135M decode kernel -15-25%, 1.7B -8-12% [uncertain]; removes ~150-180 barriers per call
recommended_actions.files_to_touch: src/megabake/codegen.py (table driver loop 1395-1431, phase_rows), src/megabake/runtime.py (wait_for_event polling, ready buffer layout), src/megabake/schedule.py (region events per interval), src/megabake/memory.py (workspace lifetimes keyed to events instead of barriers), src/megabake/compiler.py (default scheduler)
recommended_actions.prerequisite: Workspace lifetime analysis must express 'freed after event e completes for epoch k' instead of 'freed at barrier'

recommended_actions.action: Lower tile-level prerequisites (make_event_schedule) to compact events with MPK-style grouping: GCD of producer/consumer partitions per edge, LCM at fork/join, and contiguous consumer ranges after linearizing task order. Store a per-CTA task list (static, round-robin like MPK) as a device table of (phase, tile, wait_event, publish_event).
recommended_actions.expected_gain: Additional 3-8% on 135M, 2-4% on 1.7B decode; enables partial attention start per KV head [uncertain]
recommended_actions.files_to_touch: src/megabake/schedule.py (_tile_prerequisites, make_event_schedule), src/megabake/codegen.py (per-task table emission), src/megabake/plan.py
recommended_actions.prerequisite: Phase-level events in the table launch (previous action)

recommended_actions.action: While a CTA waits on an event, issue cp.async.bulk.prefetch.L2 for the weight tiles of its next GEMM task (ROADMAP step 9). Bound the prefetch to an L2 budget derived from TargetFacts.
recommended_actions.prerequisite: Events in table launch; target fact for L2 size

recommended_actions.action: Make thresholds target-derived: replace SWAP_AB_MAX_ROWS, split-K limits, fold limits and _TABLE_LAUNCH_OPS gating with cost-model or measured decisions using TargetFacts. Re-test split-K and swapAB on a full-SM H100/H200 or another MIG profile before claiming defaults.
recommended_actions.expected_gain: Avoids regressions on other GPUs; no direct speedup on the current slice
recommended_actions.prerequisite: Access to a second hardware configuration

recommended_actions.action: Generic horizontal fusion: concatenate weights of GEMMs that share an input and have no dependency between them (q/k/v, gate/up), mirroring MPK's fused qkv and gate_up weights but derived from the graph, not a builder.
recommended_actions.expected_gain: Fewer under-filled GEMM phases; about 2 fewer phases per layer; estimated -3-6% decode kernel [uncertain]
recommended_actions.prerequisite: Weight concatenation at compile time with aliasing checks

recommended_actions.action: Runtime token count: compile a bucket for max tokens and pass the actual token count (and qo_indptr for batched requests) as a device value read by bodies. Tiles beyond the count exit early, as MPK tasks do.
recommended_actions.expected_gain: Removes up to 2x padding waste at bucket edges; reduces number of compiled buckets
recommended_actions.prerequisite: Bodies that tolerate a runtime row count (GEMM TMA bounds, attention masks)

recommended_actions.action: Optional multi-step persistent decode: keep the kernel resident across N decode steps with on-device argmax/sampling, a pinned stop flag and device-side KV length advance (MPK offline mode pattern).
recommended_actions.expected_gain: Removes ~0.5-0.65 ms host plus Dynamo cost per token on small models (15-30% of complete call)
recommended_actions.prerequisite: Sampling and stop condition expressible in the captured graph; events (so iteration boundaries need no host)

recommended_actions.action: Batch-prefetch upcoming phase_table rows and TMA descriptors into shared memory (MPK loads up to 16 TaskDescs per cp.async batch) once per-task tables exist.
recommended_actions.expected_gain: Small (<1-2%), hides table reads behind compute
